label: Supplier certification
summary: Onboarding records the classification the client (Saudi Aramco or SABIC) assigned, the standard version, the certificate type and whether this is a first certification or a renewal; the audit firm's validation and the evidence work start after onboarding.

source.ref: Aramco CCC program page (classifications decide the control set; CCC and CCC+; certificate valid two years) and SABIC CyberTrust program page

fields.label: Standard version

source.ref: Library file cites SACS-002; SmartSuite (secondary only) says SACS-210 replaced it in 2026; the Aramco text could not be read

fields.note: Record the standard and version the Aramco contract names. The library file cites SACS-002 but a secondary source says SACS-210 replaced it in 2026 (unverified). The contract decides which one applies.

fields.label: Standard version

source.ref: The library holds one current SABIC CyberTrust edition; which edition is in force was not confirmed

fields.note: Record the version of the SABIC CyberTrust standard the contract names. The edition in force was not confirmed (unverified); SABIC decides which edition applies.

fields.label: Classifications
fields.note: Aramco's classification decides which controls apply. Record the classes Aramco gave in the contract or its portal, using its wording. The client confirms them; the supplier does not choose them.

fields.label: Classifications

source.ref: SABIC supplier page says classification decides the control set; these class names come from the library's file and were not confirmed on SABIC's pages

fields.note: SABIC's classification also decides the controls. These class names come from the library's file and were not confirmed on SABIC's pages (unverified); SABIC confirms which apply.

fields.label: Client confirmed

source.ref: A client-signed classification letter is part of the planned design; the form Aramco or SABIC use was not confirmed

fields.note: Tick when the client has already confirmed the classification in writing. Whether that is a signed letter or a portal record was not confirmed (unverified); keep the document.

source.ref: Aramco CCC program page and SABIC CyberTrust program page: validation by an authorised audit firm; certificate valid two years

fields.label: Certificate type
fields.note: CCC is a self-assessment with a remote check; CCC+ adds an on-site assessment. Aramco requires CCC+ for the Network Connectivity and Critical Data Processor classifications. Choose from what Aramco told you.

fields.label: Certificate status
fields.note: A first certification, a renewal and a recertification after a lapse follow different routes. Certificates are valid for two years.

fields.label: Certificate file
fields.note: Optional: attach the current certificate. It is kept in Evidence.

gate.label: The client has confirmed the classification
gate.hint: Ask the client to confirm the classification in writing; it decides the controls.

gate.label: CCC or CCC+ is decided
gate.hint: Network Connectivity and Critical Data Processor need CCC+ (on-site). Ask Aramco if unsure.

gate.label: Network Connectivity needs the CCC+ certificate
gate.hint: Network Connectivity and Critical Data Processor are assessed on site: choose CCC+.

gate.label: Critical Data Processor needs the CCC+ certificate
gate.hint: Network Connectivity and Critical Data Processor are assessed on site: choose CCC+.
